size.note: Newman's Birds gives 55–63 cm. The female is larger than the male. Newman also gives a mass of 1.2–2 kg.

habitat: Solitary at coastal bays, estuaries and lagoons, or at large inland waters. It perches over or near water on a post, branch or rock.
summary: An uncommon summer Palearctic visitor, with some overwintering. Dark above, with a slightly crested head and a facial mask, and white below. The legs are white and the wings are long. The breast-band is often vestigial, and strongest in the immature. In flight the underwing has a bold dark carpal patch and a dark central bar, and the tail is well banded. It is normally silent. The call is a shrill whistle. Newman names no months. The Kemp code NB was left unchanged.

calls.description: Normally silent. The call is a shrill whistle. Grade A call from Orlando Wetlands, Florida. No openly licensed southern African grade A call outranked it. The filename is XC143656-Osprey FL, Orlando Wetlands, July 18, 2013, 0703 AM.mp3.

research.note: Newman calls it an uncommon summer Palearctic visitor, with some overwintering, and names no months. Status is palearctic-migrant and monthsPresent is unset. The overwintering birds and the incomplete immature plumage are why this needs review. African Fish-Eagle is the comparison Newman names and is not described here as a difference. Population figures and the Kemp code NB were left unchanged.
